chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah, Exalted is He, support him—narrated to me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who applies nūrah, then puts flour with oil, mixing it with it, and rubs himself with it after the nūrah to remove its smell. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

Then he said—may Allah, Exalted is He, support him: Tayammum is not performed with zarnīkh, because it is a mineral and not earth, such that what lies above it would be dust. This also is like what has preceded, because when the obligation of tayammum with that to which the unrestricted name of dust applies is established, then everything to which the name of dust does not apply in an absolute sense is not permissible for tayammum.

Then he said—may Allah, Exalted is He, support him: If a person finds himself in muddy land while needing to perform tayammum and does not find dust, then let him shake his garment, or the mane of his riding animal, or the felt of his saddle, or his pack-saddle. If dust comes out from any of that, he performs tayammum with it. If no dust comes out from them, then let him place his hands upon the mud, then raise them and wipe one upon the other until no wetness remains in them, and wipe with them his face and the outer sides of his palms.

(543) 17. That is indicated by what the Shaykh narrated to me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“If you are in a situation where you can manage nothing but clay, then perform tayammum with it, for Allah is more deserving of accepting the excuse when you do not have with you a dry garment or felt that you are able to shake out and perform tayammum with.”

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl under certain conditions
key_terms.التُّرَابِ: dust or earth, the principal valid material for tayammum
key_terms.الدَّقِيقَ: flour mixed with oil and used here after nūrah
key_terms.الزِّرْنِيخِ: a mineral substance with which tayammum is not permitted here
key_terms.النُّورَةِ: depilatory lime used for hair removal
key_terms.الْوَحَلِ: mud, used for tayammum when no dust is available
key_terms.غَبَرَةٌ: dust shaken out from cloth or gear for tayammum
key_terms.لِبْدٌ: felt, from which dust may be shaken for tayammum

ai.seo_question: Can tayammum be performed with mud or minerals when dust is unavailable?
ai.summary: This passage discusses legal rulings related to tayammum and the permissibility of using certain substances. It states that tayammum is valid with dust and, in constrained circumstances, with mud when no dust can be found, while it is not valid with minerals such as zarnīkh. It also includes a brief ruling that there is no harm in using a flour-and-oil mixture after nūrah to remove its odor.
